findings.description: The bucket is explicitly documented as public and has no ACL restriction, no bucket policy restriction, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so anonymous read (and potentially list) access to its objects is possible. It stores a customer master file.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a KMS customer-managed key as the other log bucket is.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this internet-exposed bucket leaves no S3 access audit trail, preventing detection or investigation of data exfiltration.
Versioning is disabled, so objects overwritten or deleted (accidentally, or maliciously via the public access path) cannot be recovered.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A file named customer-master.xlsx (clearly sensitive customer data) is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and has no default encryption; no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption is set on the object either.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest under a managed key.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial records, leaving no audit trail of object access.
Versioning is not enabled, so deletion or overwrite of financial objects is unrecoverable and tampering is not detectable.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data at rest in this bucket is not protected by an explicitly configured (ideally customer-managed) key.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket is not recorded for audit or incident response.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving stored datasets without enforced encryption at rest.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects may be read or written over plaintext HTTP.
No bucket policy denies non-TLS (aws:SecureTransport false) requests, permitting financial data to traverse the network unencrypted.
The log bucket encrypts at rest with KMS but has no policy requiring TLS (aws:SecureTransport) for access, so log data can be retrieved over plaintext HTTP.
